name: Word of Wisdom
originalWord: λόγος σοφίας (lógos sophías, Gr.); חָכְמָה (chokhmáh, Hebr.)
meaning: Supernatural word revealing God's plan or solution

questions.text: In conflicts, I have already been given a solution that immediately ended the dispute (cf. Solomon's judgment, 1 Kgs 3).
I have already been able to apply complex biblical principles to a very practical everyday situation.
In precarious situations, words came to mind that opponents had nothing to counter (cf. Lk 21:15).
I urge to understand God's hidden plans for the future of our congregation.
It is important to me to find divine strategies instead of human compromises for stuck problems.
Others say that my advice has helped them to see God's will clearly in crises.
Through my contributions in meetings
Does the person offer solutions in stuck situations that restore peace?
Have you experienced that this person's advice led to good results in the long term?

name: Word of Knowledge
meaning: Supernatural knowledge or insight into God's secrets

questions.text: I already knew things about a person's life circumstances that I could not know naturally (cf. John 4:17-18).
God gave me a specific image or word for another person's situation during prayer.
While reading the Bible, I suddenly understood a deep connection that was previously completely hidden from me.
I have the desire for God to reveal secrets to me in order to serve people more specifically.
I like to search deep in the Scriptures to raise the treasures of knowledge (cf. Col 2:3).
People are often shaken or deeply moved because I address things that only God could know.
My insights have led to hidden sins or blockages coming to light and healing beginning.

name: Faith
meaning: Special, miracle-working faith that moves mountains

questions.text: I stayed calm in situations where everyone else despaired because I knew for sure that God would intervene.
I prayed for impossible things and saw God make them come true against all logic.
I have already taken steps (financial or professional) that were based only on trust in God's promise.
I want to initiate projects for which no visible resources are currently available.
I am bored by security; I want to see God bring down walls through our trust.
My unwavering trust has encouraged others to believe anew in God's miracles.
By holding on to God's promise, goals were achieved that the team/congregation had long given up on.
Following my prayer
I often feel a physical empathy (e.g. heat or tingling) when God wants to heal someone.
I have experienced how prayer healed not only physical but also deep emotional wounds.
I feel a strong urge to lay hands on sick people in the hospital or at home.
I firmly believe that Jesus still heals today just as he did in the time of the apostles.
Sick people regularly report to me that they feel much better or are pain-free after my prayer.
My ministry has led to doctors marveling at the unexpected recovery of patients.
I have experienced how laws of nature were overridden through prayer.
God worked signs through me that left outsiders awe-struck or marvelling.
I have witnessed how a situation was immediately and visibly changed by a prayer of mine.
I have the deep confidence that God still performs visible signs of his power today to confirm his word.
I don't just want to talk about God, but see his power in concrete action.
People around me have found faith through visible acts of power from God.
My ministry is often accompanied by extraordinary occurrences that are not humanly explainable.
Do extraordinary
Do these events lead to outsiders giving God the glory or finding faith?
I have already passed on messages that revealed someone's hidden thoughts (cf. 1 Cor 14:24-25).
God has already given me specific warnings or hints for the future (cf. Agabus, Acts 11:28).
When I speak, I often feel that it is not my own thoughts, but an impulse from above.
I am burning to tell the congregation what is important to God right now in this moment.
It is a concern of mine to edify, comfort, and exhort people through divine revelation (1 Cor 14:3).
People often say to me: How did you know that? That's exactly what God already told me this morning!
My prophetic words have contributed to people taking new hope or turning back.
Does the person share impulses or impressions that fit exactly into the current life situation of others?
Do people feel corrected
I was already able to recognize whether a spiritual manifestation was real or a deception (cf. 1 John 4:1).
I have already perceived when someone pretended to act in God's name with false motives (cf. Acts 16:16-18).
I often instinctively feel which atmosphere (e.g. occultism, pride or holiness) dominates a assembly.
I feel a high responsibility to protect the congregation from deceptive influences.
I want to look behind the scenes of the visible world to understand the spiritual causes of problems.
The church leadership values my judgment when it comes to testing new teachings or trends.
Through my vigilance
Does the person warn in good time against unhealthy spiritual influences or false motives?
Does the person's assessment of the authenticity of a situation prove to be correct in retrospect?
I regularly pray in a language I never learned (cf. Acts 2:4).
When I pray in tongues, I notice how my inner man is strengthened and edified (1 Cor 14:4).
I have experienced how my prayer in tongues led to interpretation in a public assembly.
I have the desire to communicate with God in prayer beyond my understanding.
I want to use this gift to speak out God's mysteries in the Spirit (1 Cor 14:2).
My prayer life has gained a new depth and passion through this gift.
When I speak publicly in tongues (and it is interpreted), the congregation perceives this as a direct message from God.
Does the person use speaking in tongues in a way that contributes to edification?
When the person speaks publicly in tongues
When someone prays in tongues
I have already experienced how my interpretation was exactly the answer to another person's prayer.
I have the courage to stand up in an assembly and speak out the interpretation of a prayer in tongues loudly.
I pray that God gives me the gift to make the incomprehensible understandable for the congregation.
It is important to me that the gifts of speaking in tongues serve the edification of all and do not confuse (1 Cor 14:26).
After my interpretation
The congregation is specifically encouraged or corrected in God's truth through my interpretation.
Can the person interpret speaking in tongues in such a way that the content becomes understandable for everyone?
Is the congregation specifically strengthened in faith through this person's interpretations?
I have often taken on tasks in the background so that others could do their ministry better (cf. Acts 6:1-7).
I discover practical necessities (repairs, preparations) that others often overlook.
It gives me joy to relieve people quite practically without my name being mentioned.
I would rather help actively than lead long theoretical discussions.
I want everything in the congregation to run smoothly and I tackle everything wherever help is needed.
Leaders often tell me that I am an indispensable support for them in the everyday life of the congregation.
By my tackling
Does the person readily take on practical tasks that arise in the background?
Would the practical work of the congregation suffer noticeably if this person stopped their service?
When I explain the Bible, others say that they suddenly understand complex topics (cf. Acts 18:24-26).
I spend a lot of time studying the Scriptures in order to pass on the truth systematically.
I have experienced how false teachings in a group were corrected through my instruction.
I have a burning desire for Christians to grow in their faith through sound knowledge.
I am enthusiastic about researching biblical connections and processing them logically.
People report that they have found a more stable foundation for their life through my teaching.
The group I teach shows a clear growth in spiritual maturity and knowledge.
Can the person explain biblical content in such a way that it is easily understandable and logically comprehensible?
Do you observe that listeners have a deeper understanding of the truth after his/her explanations?
I have already helped people out of deepest despondency (cf. Barnabas, the son of encouragement, Acts 4:36).
I often find exactly the right words to motivate someone not to give up in a crisis.
I have pointed out blind spots to people lovingly but directly
I want to help people reach their full potential in God.
I cannot watch when siblings resign; I simply have to encourage them.
People specifically come to me when they need a spiritual strengthening or a motivational boost.
After conversations with me
Does the person actively approach people to comfort
Do people feel strengthened and empowered to move on after a conversation with this person?
I have already given amounts of money anonymously and generously to alleviate a need (cf. Acts 4:34-37).
God has already entrusted me with unexpected resources that I could directly pass on into the kingdom of God.
I experienced how my financial sacrifice only made an important missionary work possible.
I see my money and my possessions primary as tools for God's kingdom, not for my luxury.
It gives me great joy to finance generous projects when I am convinced of their purpose.
Through my gifts
Others feel encouraged by my generosity to be more trusting with their own finances themselves.
Does the person act above-average generously with their possessions or money to alleviate need?
Are bottlenecks in the church work solved through the financial or material help of this person?
I have already coordinated teams or projects in such a way that everyone could use their gifts optimally (cf. Tit 1:5).
In confusing situations, I keep an overview and set the direction (cf. the helmsman, 1 Cor 12:28).
I have experienced how chaos in the church work was eliminated through my planning.
It motivates me to translate visions into concrete
I want to take responsibility so that the congregation achieves its goals effectively.
People like to follow my leadership because they feel safe and well-led through my structure.
Under my responsibility
Does the person coordinate tasks and people so that goals are achieved effectively and in an orderly manner?
Do people trust this person's organization because it conveys clarity and security?
I have already taken care of people intensively who were shunned by everyone else (cf. Lk 10:33-35).
I often spend time with the grieving or sick without it exhausting me emotionally.
I have already alleviated need quite practically by simply being there and suffering with them.
My heart bleeds when I see injustice or loneliness; I must then act.
I want to show the love of Jesus especially to those who are on the fringes of society.
People in crises often tell me that my presence has given them new courage for life.
Through my service
Does the person specifically seek proximity to those suffering
Do people experience deep emotional healing and acceptance through this person's attention?
I have already helped to found a new group or congregation where there was nothing before (pioneer work).
I have experienced a spiritual authority that enabled me to equip leaders in other congregations.
God has already sent me into completely foreign cultures or environments to lay the foundation of faith there.
I feel the urge to constantly open up new spiritual terrains instead of just managing what already exists.
I carry a burden for the global church and the cooperation of different congregations.
There are congregations or ministries that exist today because I dared to take the courageous first step.
Other leaders recognize my supra-regional responsibility and seek my advice for their works.
Does the person successfully initiate new projects or foundations (pioneering spirit)?
Does the person possess a recognized spiritual authority over different groups or congregations?
I have already experienced how people spontaneously entrusted their life to Jesus after a conversation with me.
I always find natural ways to get into conversation about faith with people far from church.
I have already spoken before groups of unbelievers and felt a special authority while doing so.
It burns in my soul that people are lost without Jesus (cf. Rom 9:2-3).
I am constantly looking for new methods to communicate the Gospel in a contemporary and understandable way.
In my environment
I motivate the congregation to direct its focus more strongly again towards the people outside.
Does the person actively and fearlessly seek conversation with people who do not yet know Jesus?
Have you witnessed people taking steps towards faith through this person's influence?
I accompany people over years in their spiritual growth and help them through valleys.
I have already looked for strayed siblings and lovingly led them back into the community (cf. Ezek 34:16).
I actively protect the group for which I am responsible from negative influences or division.
I have a deep interest in the long-term development and well-being of individual persons.
I want to create an atmosphere in which people feel spiritually safe and at home.
People trust me with their deepest needs because they know that I stand up for them.
The group I care for is characterized by strong cohesion and mutual care.
Does the person care for the spiritual well-being of a group long-term and reliably?
Does the group cared for by this person develop a strong community and spiritual maturity?
